name: MigrationPro
summary: Shopify app that imports products, customers, orders, collections, URLs and 301 redirects from WooCommerce, Wix, Magento and 30-odd other platforms.
best_for: merchants moving an existing store into Shopify who want products, customers, orders and, critically, URLs and 301 redirects preserved, who are willing to pay the $29 add-on that carries those redirects on the self-service route, and who would rather pay once than subscribe to a tool they will use for a week
skip_if: you are migrating away from Shopify or between two other platforms, since this only imports into Shopify; or you want one firm number before you start, because the price still depends on your record counts and on which of the priced add-ons your source platform turns out to need
honest_knock:
Start with the listing, because it went away and came back. On 5 October 2026 the Shopify App Store listing said the app was not currently available, with no install button and no review page; on 17 November 2026 it was live again with an Install button and 190 reviews, and the app installed normally in our own test. The vendor has not said why the listing was unavailable.

The listing tells you nothing about what this costs: “Free to install. Additional charges may apply”, and a single plan block saying pricing is tailored to the entities you migrate. The number lives on the vendor's calculator, and the first number you find there, $29, is the floor for the smallest store on the self-service route, not the price for yours. Their own homepage says a typical store lands between $49 and $299. Run the calculator before you form an opinion about value.

The add-on structure used to be the unknowable part, and as of 18 September 2026 it is not: the pricing page lists every add-on with a price, from $19 to $39, and marks all of them included on the managed plan. That is a real improvement in what a buyer can read before committing. It also makes the self-service route look less like $29: the 301 redirects add-on, which is the one thing a migrating store can least afford to get wrong, is a $29 extra on a $29 migration.

The marketing still runs ahead of the evidence. The pricing page says “Trusted by 250,000+ stores”, the homepage uses the same figure for migrations, and the FAQ says 250,000+ migrations over 13 years: one number doing three different jobs. The same page, and an FAQ answer saying the app is available on the Shopify App Store, still claim 5.0 from 170+ verified reviews, against a listing that showed 186 on 18 September, of which 181 were five star, 4 four star and one a single star, and 190 on 17 November 2026. Those reviews were good; weigh them rather than the banner.

One practical limit sits in the reviews rather than the marketing. The FAQ says most stores finish in one to three hours and that 10,000+ products may take longer but still complete the same day, while a merchant migrating a very large catalogue in July 2026 wrote plainly that large volumes take a very long time and that the team helped speed it up. If you are moving tens of thousands of records, let the free demo and your own record count decide which of those two you are, not the FAQ.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/migrationpro-shopify-migration-app and in our own test the same day; migrationpro.io/pricing/ read 2026-10-05) The self run migration starts at $29 and the done for you plan at $300, both one time payments, and the Shopify App Store listing is live again with an Install button. On 5 October 2026 the listing read “This app is not currently available on the Shopify App Store”, with no install button and a reviews page that answered 404; on 17 November 2026 it showed one plan again, free to install, with the line that pricing is tailored to the entities you migrate and no subscription fees, billed in USD, and 190 reviews averaging 5.0. In our own test that day the app installed normally, and its checkout for a 2 product demo store quoted $29 as a one time payment, by card through Stripe or by PayPal, outside Shopify billing. The numbers live on the vendor's own pricing page, which quotes on your product, customer and order counts. Two routes are sold there, both one-time payments rather than subscriptions. The Automated app plan, where you run the migration yourself, starts at $29 based on store size. The Done-for-you plan, where their team handles mapping, testing and go-live with a dedicated specialist, starts at $300 with every add-on included. Both carry a 30-day guarantee, need no credit card, and begin with a free demo of up to 10 products, customers and orders. What has changed since 23 August is the add-on table: each one now carries a price. 301 redirects, order ID preservation, categories mapped to automated collections and content images are $29 each; customer groups to tags and default stock quantity are $19 each; spam customer detection, active products only and tax-inclusive pricing are $39 each; merging short and long descriptions, generating variants from options and resetting the target store are free. The homepage puts a typical store at $49 to $299 on actual record counts, and the FAQ says most stores finish in one to three hours, with 10,000+ products taking longer but still completing the same day. The app is English-only, migrates from WooCommerce, Wix, Squarespace, BigCommerce, Magento, PrestaShop, OpenCart, Shopware, Etsy, Amazon, CSV and Excel among others, and covers products, customers, orders, collections, images, URLs and 301 redirects, with Smart Sync to re-import data changed during the run. Developer Migrationpro, LLC, Dover, Delaware; the app launched 10 May 2022, and on 18 September 2026 it carried 186 reviews averaging 5.0, 181 five star, 4 four star and one at a single star; on 17 November 2026 it carried 190, 185 of them five star. Note that migrationpro.io/pricing without the trailing slash now answers 308.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested MigrationPro on a Shopify development store: the install, the external dashboard, the choice of source platforms, a free demo migration of 2 made-up products from a self-made CSV file with an invented source address (done in about 2 minutes 10 seconds, with the products left Active in the store), the paid options, the one-time checkout of $29 (not paid) and the All-In-One package (not entered), and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid. Listing and install: the App Store listing MigrationPro: Store Migration shows a rating of 5.0 (190) and Free to install. Additional charges may apply. The dossier said (5 October) that the listing had been withdrawn; it is now installable. The install button opened a pop-up to the Shopify grant screen for MP - Store Migration & Import with View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the install was approved at 14:51. After the install the app opened straight on an external dashboard, app.migrationpro.io, logged in through Shopify, with no separate account asked. A message Finish setting up your account (confirm a notification email and choose a company type) was not followed. A vendor live chat widget opened by itself and showed messages; we sent nothing. Core action, a demo migration, about 2 minutes 10 seconds from the install (14:51 to about 14:53:40) and more than 12 steps, partly because we had to make a file and invent a source address: Create New Migration offers 52 source platforms (among them WooCommerce, PrestaShop, Wix and CSV); for most platforms a real source URL and a connector file (mp_connector.zip, to upload by FTP) are needed, which was not possible without a source store. We chose the source CSV, which asks for a Source Store URL (required) and CSV files (Categories, Products, Product Variants, Customers, Orders, Order Items, Blog Posts, Blog Comments, CMS Pages, Discounts). There is no built-in demo or test source. We used a Products.csv that we made ourselves with 2 made-up products (Demo Mug and Demo Shirt) and the address https://example.com as source URL; no login details were entered. In the Configure step we ticked Products. Paid options: Migrate Only Active Products ($39), Migrate Content Images from Products, Categories, CMS pages and Blog Posts ($29), Implement 301 Redirects in Target Store Post-Migration ($29), Convert Categories to Shopify Automated Collections ($29), Set Out-of-Stock Product Quantity to 100 in Target Store ($19) and Calculate Product Price with Tax ($39); free options: Target Store Data Reset, Generate Product Variants from Option Combinations and Consolidate Short and Full Descriptions; none was switched on. The CSV Headers Mapping filled in name, description and price by itself. The button Next: Run Free Demo Migration was pressed at 14:53:31 and after about 10 seconds the page said Demo migration complete. Please review your data and proceed with full migration. with the table Products 2/2. In the Shopify admin, Demo Shirt and Demo Mug appeared as Active products, with our store name as vendor. This is a demo of two made-up products from a CSV with an invented source address; a real migration from a real source store was not tested. Plans and checkout: there is no Shopify subscription screen, no Approve subscription and no test charge; payment runs outside Shopify. The checkout page of the migration shows Entities $29, Enabled Additional Migration Options $0, Additional development $0, Order total $29, the note This is one-time payment only, a Discount code field, and the payment methods Credit card (Pay with credit card via Stripe) or PayPal (Pay with your PayPal account) with a Place order button, which we did not press because it is a real payment. The price depends on the number of records: 2 products gave $29; the pricing page has a calculator (products, customers, orders) that we did not use. The All-In-One Migration Package (A dedicated Personal Assistant will handle all aspects) is priced at $300 with Estimated time - 1 day and starts with a Consultation with the vendor experts; we did not go further because it means a conversation. Cancelling: there is no subscription to cancel, because the payment is one-time. The app was uninstalled via Settings, Apps and Uninstall; the dialog says that a request will be sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information, and asks for a reason and optional feedback; we gave Testing multiple apps at 14:58 and the app left the installed list. Not tested: a real migration from a source store, 301 redirects, images, customers and orders, Smart Sync, the payment, the All-In-One package with its consultation, the live chat and confirming the notification email. Clean up: the two demo products Demo Shirt and Demo Mug are still Active in the store and were not deleted; the app was uninstalled; a helper file with the CSV was kept outside the project; one pop-up tab of the first install attempt could not be closed with our tools. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: There is no built-in test source, so a source address and a CSV file had to be made up for the demo; most platforms need a connector file uploaded by FTP; the price depends on the number of records; and a vendor chat opened by itself.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. The dossier said (5 October) that the listing had been withdrawn; it is now installable. The install button opened a pop-up to the Shopify grant screen for MP - Store Migration & Import with View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the install was approved at 14:51. After the install the app opened straight on an external dashboard, app.migrationpro.io, logged in through Shopify, with no separate account asked. A message Finish setting up your account (confirm a notification email and choose a company type) was not followed. A vendor live chat widget opened by itself and showed messages; we sent nothing. We chose the source CSV, which asks for a Source Store URL (required) and CSV files (Categories, Products, Product Variants, Customers, Orders, Order Items, Blog Posts, Blog Comments, CMS Pages, Discounts). There is no built-in demo or test source.
